test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 19 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.**

The detective told the witnesses that they must tell him everything they had seen that morning, as it could be the key to solving the case that had been haunting the city for a long time.

options.text: "You must tell me everything you saw this morning, as it could be the key to solving the case that has been haunting the city for a long time," the detective said to the witnesses.
"You had to tell me everything you saw this morning, as it could be the key to solving the case that was haunting the city for a long time," the detective said to the witnesses.
"You must tell me everything you had seen that morning, as it could be the key to solving the case that had been haunting the city for a long time," the detective said to the witnesses.
"You must tell him everything you saw this morning, as it could be the key to solving the case that has been haunting the city for a long time," the detective said to the witnesses.

solution: The correct answer is '1' i.e. "You must tell me everything you saw this morning, as it could be the key to solving the case that has been haunting the city for a long time," the detective said to the witnesses . [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The question is about converting an indirect speech into direct speech. • The sentence in indirect speech states that "The detective told the witnesses that they must tell him everything they had seen that morning, as it could be the key to solving the case." The verb "must" in direct speech remains "must" as it indicates obligation in the present tense. • The pronouns and verbs must be adjusted to match direct speech: • “they” becomes “you” since the detective is addressing the witnesses directly. • “had seen” becomes “saw” because in direct speech, the past perfect tense is often converted into the simple past tense to reflect the immediacy of the conversation. • Options 2, 3, and 4 fail to accurately reflect the correct structure and verb usage for direct speech: • Option 2 incorrectly uses "had to tell," which changes the meaning. • Option 3 uses “had seen that morning,” which is unnecessary for direct speech. • Option 4 incorrectly uses "tell him," which is inconsistent with the direct address in direct speech. Correct sentence: *"You must tell me everything you saw this morning, as it could be the key to solving the case that has been haunting the city for a long time," the detective said to the witnesses.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** • **Direct and Indirect Speech Rules:** • In direct speech, the exact words of the speaker are quoted and enclosed in quotation marks. • In indirect speech, the speaker's words are reported without quotation marks, and pronouns, tenses, and adverbs of time/place are adjusted accordingly. • **Examples:** • Direct: He said, "I am going to the market now." • Indirect: He said that he was going to the market then. 4a:Ta1a,
